hints: Calculate the total age of the first group: $12 \times 48.7$.
Calculate the total age of the second group: $7 \times 38.1$.
Add the two totals together and divide by the combined number of people $12 + 7 = 19$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand combined means.
The mean of a combined sample is the total sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations:
$$\bar{z} = \frac{\sum x + \sum y}{n_x + n_y}$$

Step 2: Find the sum of ages for each class:
- First class: $n_x = 12$ people with mean $\bar{x} = 48.7$ years:
$$\sum x = n_x \bar{x} = 12 \times 48.7 = 584.4$$
- Second class: $n_y = 7$ people with mean $\bar{y} = 38.1$ years:
$$\sum y = n_y \bar{y} = 7 \times 38.1 = 266.7$$

Step 3: Combine sums and divide by total headcount $n = 12 + 7 = 19$:
$$\sum z = 584.4 + 266.7 = 851.1$$
$$\bar{z} = \frac{851.1}{19} \approx 44.7947 \approx 44.8\text{ years}$$

hints: Rearrange the variance formula $\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2$ to find $\sum x^2 = n(\sigma^2 + \bar{x}^2)$.
Calculate $\sum x^2$ for the first class and $\sum y^2$ for the second class.
Add the sums of squares to get $\sum z^2 = \sum x^2 + \sum y^2$, and substitute into the combined standard deviation formula $\sqrt{\frac{\sum z^2}{19} - \bar{z}^2}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Express the variance formula for raw data:
$$\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2 \implies \sum x^2 = n(\sigma^2 + \bar{x}^2)$$

Step 4: Pool the sums of squares for all $19$ people:
$$\sum z^2 = \sum x^2 + \sum y^2 = 29162.55 + 10284.75 = 39447.30$$

Step 6: Take the square root:
$$\sigma_{\text{combined}} = \sqrt{69.60520} \approx 8.3669 \approx 8.37\text{ years}$$
